parentSettingsBehavior.description: Choose whether Claude Code applies managed settings supplied by an embedding host process, such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension, when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present. With `"first-wins"`, Claude Code drops the host-supplied settings; with `"merge"`, it applies them under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. Set `"merge"` when a host needs to pass its own restrictions to the sessions it launches, for example Claude Desktop delivering a gateway's egress allowlist.
parentSettingsBehavior.scope_note: Claude Code reads it from the highest-priority admin-controlled managed source.

permissionExplainerEnabled.description: > [!WARNING] > > Removed in v2.1.257, together with the `Ctrl+E` command explanation on Bash and PowerShell permission prompts. Setting it has no effect on current versions.

permissions.description: Control which tools Claude can use without asking, which ones prompt, and which ones are blocked. Also set the default permission mode for new sessions. Every `permissions.*` key below nests under this object.

permissions.additionalDirectories.description: Give Claude file access to directories outside the one you started in, as additional working directories. Most `.claude/` configuration is not discovered from these directories.

permissions.allow.description: List the tool uses Claude Code approves without asking you. In an MCP rule, `*` can appear only in the tool name after the `mcp__<server>__` prefix, such as `mcp__github__get_*`; it can't appear in the server name.

permissions.ask.description: List the tool uses that prompt you for confirmation even in a permission mode that would otherwise approve them, such as `acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions`. In `dontAsk` mode Claude Code denies a matching tool use instead of prompting.

permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDire.default: unset, so reads outside the working directories follow your permission mode
permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDire.description: Make Claude's file tools refuse reads outside your working directories in every permission mode, including `bypassPermissions`. Claude Code denies `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, and `LSP` calls on those paths and tells Claude to ask you to add the directory with `/add-dir`. Files Claude Code itself needs stay readable, such as your skills, plugins, rules, agents, commands, and the `CLAUDE.md` memory file under `~/.claude/`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.
permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDire.scope_note: A `true` in any file applies, so a repository can turn the block on for itself but can't lift yours.

permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDir.default: unset, so writes outside the working directories follow your permission mode. The block is also on while Claude Code can't read the `permissions` object in your managed settings.
permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDir.description: Make the `Write`, `Edit`, and `NotebookEdit` tools refuse paths outside your working directories in every permission mode, including `bypassPermissions`, apart from some of Claude Code's own files. The key doesn't limit shell commands, MCP tools, or the programs hooks run. To limit where shell commands write, turn on sandboxing. Requires Claude Code v2.1.314 or later.
permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDir.scope_note: A `true` in any file the session loads applies, so a repository can turn the block on for itself but can't lift yours. In a cloud session, Claude Code might not apply the key, because the file tools run in a container that is itself the boundary.

permissions.defaultMode.description: Set the default permission mode for new sessions. When you leave it unset, the built-in default for your surface applies.
permissions.defaultMode.scope_note: `auto` and `bypassPermissions` don't take effect from project or local settings, so set them in `~/.claude/settings.json` instead. Before v2.1.257, `bypassPermissions` took effect from any file. For conversations the VS Code extension starts, Claude Code reads only user, managed, and `--settings` values.

permissions.deny.description: List the tool uses Claude Code blocks. Use it for files that hold API keys, secrets, or environment values: Claude Code excludes matching files from file discovery and search results, denies reads of them, and blocks the Edit and Write tools on the matching paths.

permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode.description: Prevent anyone from entering `bypassPermissions` mode. Claude Code then rejects the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag, and ignores an agent definition's `permissionMode: bypassPermissions`, so the subagent runs with the parent session's permission mode.
permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode.scope_note: Typically set in managed settings to enforce organizational policy.

plansDirectory.description: Choose where Claude Code stores the plan files it writes in plan mode. Claude Code resolves the path relative to the project root.
plansDirectory.type: string, a path relative to the project root

pluginConfigs.description: Store the non-sensitive answers you give a plugin's `userConfig` configuration dialog, keyed by plugin ID. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you fill in the dialog, so you don't need to edit it by hand. Claude Code stores sensitive options in the macOS Keychain instead, falling back to `~/.claude/.credentials.json` when the Keychain rejects the write; on platforms without a supported keychain, it stores them in `~/.claude/.credentials.json`.
pluginConfigs.type: object mapping a plugin ID to an object with an `options` field, mapping each option name to a string, number, Boolean, or array of strings, and an optional `mcpServers` field holding per-server user configuration values in the same shape

pluginSuggestionMarketplaces.default: unset, so no marketplace-declared suggestions surface
pluginSuggestionMarketplaces.description: Name the marketplaces whose plugins can appear as contextual install suggestions, in spinner tips and pinned at the top of the `/plugin` **Discover** tab. The built-in first-party frontend-design tip is unaffected. Suggestions come from each plugin's `relevance` declaration in its marketplace entry.

pluginTrustMessage.default: unset, so Claude Code shows the standard warning alone
pluginTrustMessage.description: Add your organization's own text to the plugin trust warning Claude Code shows before installation, for example to confirm that plugins from your internal marketplace are vetted.

policyHelper.description: Run an executable you deploy that computes managed settings at startup, so you can derive policy from device posture, identity, or a remote service instead of a static file. Claude Code runs the helper before it accepts the first prompt and treats the settings it emits as the managed settings for the session.
policyHelper.scope_note: Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file. Claude Code reads the key from the highest-priority managed source that carries a policy key and runs the helper only when that source is one of those three; it ignores the key in server-managed settings, the HKCU registry, and host-supplied parent settings.

policyHelper.path.description: Name the helper executable Claude Code runs. For what happens when the path breaks the rules below, see Helper failures.
policyHelper.path.scope_note: Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever `policyHelper` is read.
policyHelper.path.type: string, an absolute path in normalized form, without `.` or `..` segments; on Windows, a drive-letter or UNC path that ends in `.exe`

policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs.default: unset, so Claude Code runs the helper once at startup
policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs.description: Have Claude Code re-run the helper in the background on an interval so policy changes reach a running session. When a refresh succeeds, its output replaces the previous managed settings without a restart; when a refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the policy it already has.
policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs.scope_note: Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever `policyHelper` is read.
policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs.type: integer, milliseconds: `0` to disable refresh, otherwise at least `60000`

policyHelper.timeoutMs.description: Set how long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start.
policyHelper.timeoutMs.scope_note: Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever `policyHelper` is read.

prStatusFooterEnabled.description: Show a badge in the prompt footer for the current branch's open pull request or merge request, with a colored underline that shows its status. Appears in `/config` as **Show PR status footer**.

prUrlTemplate.description: Point the PR links Claude Code renders, in the footer badge and in tool-result summaries, at an internal code-review tool instead of `github.com`. Claude Code substitutes `{host}`, `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{number}`, and `{url}` from the PR URL. GitLab merge request links on both surfaces keep their GitLab URL.
prUrlTemplate.type: string, a URL template using any of the five placeholders

preferredNotifChannel.description: Choose how Claude Code notifies you when a task completes or a permission prompt is waiting. A mod's notifications use the same setting. Appears in `/config` as **Local notifications**.
preferredNotifChannel.scope_note: Claude Code also reads a value left in `~/.claude.json` by older versions.

prefersReducedMotion.description: Reduce or turn off interface animations such as the spinner, shimmer, and flash effects. Appears in `/config` as **Reduce motion**.

prependPlugins.description: List the managed plugins whose mods run before every mod a user installs, in the listed order. When you set this key in managed settings, name `sec-default@builtin` in the list to keep the built-in guard. In managed settings, Claude Code skips an id whose plugin doesn't count as your organization's. See Install your organization's mods and set the order for those conditions and for how the two ordering keys work together.
prependPlugins.scope_note: Claude Code reads the key from managed settings. It reads the key from user settings only on a machine with no managed settings, in a session whose credential isn't a Team or Enterprise `/login`. It ignores the key in project and local settings and in a `--settings` file.

processWrapper.default: unset, so background processes start unwrapped
processWrapper.description: On macOS and Linux, place a corporate launcher command in front of the background processes Claude Code starts. Claude Code runs the launcher with its own command line appended, so the launcher must exec into Claude Code; see Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher for the launcher contract. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later.
processWrapper.type: string, the launcher command as an argv prefix, such as an absolute path with optional arguments

promptCacheTtl.default: unset, so each main-conversation request gets its default lifetime
promptCacheTtl.description: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the main conversation. This key applies to your interactive, `-p`, and Agent SDK turns, together with the helpers Claude Code runs inline with them. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

promptSuggestionEnabled.description: Show or hide prompt suggestions, the grayed-out predictions that appear in your prompt input. Set it to `false`, or turn off **Prompt suggestions** in `/config`, to hide them.

remote.defaultEnvironmentId.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the Anthropic-hosted environment when your list has one, and otherwise the first environment in your list that isn't a Remote Control bridge environment, or the first environment when every one is a bridge environment
remote.defaultEnvironmentId.description: Pick the default cloud environment for cloud sessions you create from the CLI, such as with `claude --cloud`. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you pick an environment with `/remote-env`.
remote.defaultEnvironmentId.scope_note: For a self-hosted environment ID, user or managed settings, or the `--settings` flag only.
remote.defaultEnvironmentId.type: string, an environment ID such as `env_...` or `ccpool_...`

remoteControlAtStartup.default: unset, so the auto-connect default applies
remoteControlAtStartup.description: Connect Remote Control automatically when each interactive session starts, instead of waiting for `/remote-control`. Set it to `true` to turn auto-connect on, `false` to turn it off. Appears in `/config` as **Enable Remote Control for all sessions**.
remoteControlAtStartup.scope_note: Claude Code also reads a value left in `~/.claude.json` by older versions.

requiredMaximumVersion.description: Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization's approved method; `claude install <version>` may also work. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.
requiredMaximumVersion.scope_note: Claude Code gives no warning when it ignores the key elsewhere.
requiredMaximumVersion.type: string, a version number such as `"2.1.150"`; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored

requiredMinimumVersion.description: Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization's approved method. The check runs at startup only, so a session that's already running continues. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.
requiredMinimumVersion.scope_note: Claude Code gives no warning when it ignores the key elsewhere.
requiredMinimumVersion.type: string, a version number such as `"2.1.150"`; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored

respectGitignore.description: Control whether the `@` file picker leaves out files that match `.gitignore` patterns. Appears in `/config` as **Respect .gitignore in file picker**.
respectGitignore.scope_note: When no settings file sets it, Claude Code falls back to `respectGitignore` in `~/.claude.json`, which the `/config` toggle writes.

respondToBashCommands.description: Choose whether Claude responds after you run a shell command with the `!` prefix in the input box. By default, Claude Code adds the command's output to the conversation and Claude replies to it. Set this key to `false` to add the output to context without a reply, so you can run several commands and ask about them together.

sandbox.default: unset, so Claude Code runs commands without a sandbox
sandbox.description: Isolate the Bash commands Claude runs from your filesystem and network with sandboxing. Turn the sandbox on with `enabled`, then narrow or widen what sandboxed commands can touch with the `filesystem`, `network`, and `credentials` sub-objects. The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.
sandbox.type: object with `enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`, `excludedCommands`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `enableWeakerNestedSandbox`, `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation`, `allowAppleEvents`, `allowNestedUserNamespaces`, `bwrapPath`, `socatPath`, `ignoreViolations`, and `ripgrep`, plus the `filesystem`, `network`, and `credentials` objects

sandbox.allowAppleEvents.description: Let sandboxed commands on macOS send Apple Events, which `open`, `osascript`, and tools that open URLs in a browser need; without it they fail with error `-600`. This removes code-execution isolation: sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can send AppleScript commands to running applications such as Terminal, subject to the per-app macOS automation-consent prompt (TCC).

sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces.description: Let sandboxed commands on Linux and WSL2 create user namespaces, which Chromium's and Electron's own sandbox, a nested bubblewrap, and `unshare` need. If you set this key to `true`, you turn off a security boundary: code from a sandboxed command can end up running outside the sandbox. For rootless Podman or Buildah, use `excludedCommands` instead, because the sandbox stops them in other ways too. Requires Claude Code v2.1.305 or later.
sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces.scope_note: A `true` counts from `~/.claude/settings.json`, JSON passed with `--settings`, or managed settings. Claude Code ignores a `true` in a project's `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`. In a session with `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` set to `1`, Claude Code ignores a `true` from every source. A `false` counts from any file, by settings precedence.

sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands.description: Let Claude retry a command outside the sandbox with the `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` parameter after the sandbox blocks it. When it's `false`, Claude Code ignores that parameter. While the sandbox is running, commands Claude runs are then sandboxed unless they match an `excludedCommands` entry. The `/sandbox` **Overrides** tab shows that state as **Strict sandbox mode**. A `false` in managed settings turns on strict sandbox mode for the developers it covers.

sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed.description: Let Claude Code run sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt. Commands that can't run in the sandbox still go through the regular permission flow, and `deny` rules and content-scoped `ask` rules such as `Bash(git push *)` still apply; a bare `Bash` ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands. Set it to `false` to send sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow too, which the `/sandbox` **Mode** tab calls regular permissions mode.

sandbox.bwrapPath.default: unset, so Claude Code finds `bwrap` on `PATH`
sandbox.bwrapPath.description: Point the sandbox at a bubblewrap binary installed outside `PATH`, such as a vendored copy on an air-gapped host. Claude Code uses the path both for the startup dependency check and when it wraps each sandboxed command.
sandbox.bwrapPath.scope_note: Claude Code reads it only from managed settings so that a user, project, or local file can't point the sandbox at a different binary.
sandbox.bwrapPath.type: string, an absolute path; Claude Code drops a relative path and falls back to `PATH` lookup

sandbox.credentials.default: unset, so no credentials are protected
sandbox.credentials.description: Declare the credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands. Each entry names a file `path` or a variable `name` and a `mode`: `deny` hides the credential inside the sandbox, and `mask` shows sandboxed commands a placeholder while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests. Claude Code protects only the entries you list; there is no built-in credential deny list.
sandbox.credentials.scope_note: Claude Code honors `mask` entries, `allowPlaintextInject`, `awsPairs`, and `sigv4` only from user settings, managed settings, and the `--settings` flag.

sandbox.credentials.allowPlaintextInject.description: Allow `mask` substitution on plain HTTP requests as well as TLS-terminated HTTPS. On plain HTTP the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext, so leave this off outside trusted test networks.

sandbox.credentials.awsPairs.default: unset, so only the conventional trio is paired
sandbox.credentials.awsPairs.description: Group masked environment variables that form one AWS credential for SigV4 re-signing when your credential lives in variables with non-standard names. Claude Code links the conventional `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` trio automatically when you mask their whole values, so you need this key only for other names. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
sandbox.credentials.awsPairs.type: array of objects, each with `accessKeyIdVar`, `secretAccessKeyVar`, and optionally `sessionTokenVar`, naming `sandbox.credentials.envVars` entries

sandbox.credentials.envVars.default: unset, so no environment variables are protected
sandbox.credentials.envVars.description: Protect environment variables from sandboxed commands. With `"mode": "deny"`, Claude Code removes the variable from the environment of sandboxed commands. With `"mode": "mask"`, sandboxed commands see a per-session sentinel value, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's `injectHosts`, so tools such as `gh` and `npm` keep authenticating without ever holding the real credential.
sandbox.credentials.envVars.scope_note: Claude Code drops `mask` entries from project `.claude/settings.json` and local `.claude/settings.local.json`.
sandbox.credentials.envVars.type: array of objects, each with `name` and a `mode` of `"deny"` or `"mask"`, plus the optional mask fields for environment variables

sandbox.credentials.files.default: unset, so no credential files are protected
sandbox.credentials.files.description: Protect credential files or directories from sandboxed commands. With `"mode": "deny"`, Claude Code blocks reads of the path inside the sandbox, the same read block as `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead`. With `"mode": "mask"`, sandboxed commands on Linux and WSL2 read a sentinel copy of the file, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's `injectHosts`; on macOS the file is unreadable inside the sandbox instead. `"mode": "mask"` requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later.
sandbox.credentials.files.scope_note: Claude Code drops `mask` entries from project `.claude/settings.json` and local `.claude/settings.local.json`.
sandbox.credentials.files.type: array of objects, each with `path` and a `mode` of `"deny"` or `"mask"`, plus the optional mask fields for files

sandbox.credentials.sigv4.description: Choose what the sandbox proxy does with AWS request forms it can't re-sign: `streaming` for aws-chunked streaming uploads, `presigned` for presigned URLs, and `sigv4a` for SigV4A asymmetric signatures. This applies only to requests signed with a masked pair's placeholder access key ID. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
sandbox.credentials.sigv4.type: object with `streaming`, `presigned`, and `sigv4a`, each one of:

sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox.description: Run the Linux sandbox inside an unprivileged Docker container, where bubblewrap can't mount a fresh `/proc`. Instead the inner sandbox bind-mounts the container's existing `/proc`, which exposes process information that a fresh mount would hide. This reduces security; use it only when the outer container already provides the isolation you need.

sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation.description: Let sandboxed commands on macOS reach the system TLS trust service, `com.apple.trustd.agent`. Go-based tools such as `gh`, `gcloud`, and `terraform` need it to verify TLS certificates when you use `network.httpProxyPort` with a MITM proxy and a custom CA. This reduces security by opening a potential data exfiltration path through the trust service.

sandbox.enabled.description: Turn on sandboxing for Bash commands. When you pick a mode in the `/sandbox` panel, Claude Code writes this key to `.claude/settings.local.json` for the current project; set it in `~/.claude/settings.json` to sandbox every project.

sandbox.excludedCommands.default: unset, so no command is excluded
sandbox.excludedCommands.description: Name commands that Claude Code runs outside the sandbox, such as tools that don't work under it. Each entry uses the same syntax as the content of a `Bash(...)` permission rule: an exact command, a prefix such as `docker *`, or a wildcard pattern. A pattern with no wildcard is an exact match, so `docker` matches only `docker` with no arguments.

sandbox.failIfUnavailable.description: Make Claude Code exit with an error at startup when `sandbox.enabled` is `true` but the sandbox can't start because the platform doesn't support it or the dependency check fails. Without this key, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed. Managed deployments that require sandboxing as a security gate can use this setting.

sandbox.filesystem.default: unset, so the default read and write boundaries apply
sandbox.filesystem.description: Control which paths sandboxed commands can read and write. By default they can write to the working directory, the per-user temp directory, and directories you add with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or `permissions.additionalDirectories`, and can read the rest of the filesystem, including credential files. Widen or narrow that with the four path lists, or switch the filesystem layer off with `disabled`. See Filesystem isolation for the default boundaries.
sandbox.filesystem.type: object with `allowWrite`, `denyWrite`, `denyRead`, and `allowRead` arrays, plus the `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` and `disabled` Booleans

sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPaths.description: Honor only the `allowRead` entries that come from managed settings, so developers can't re-open read access to paths your organization blocked. Claude Code still merges `denyRead` entries from every settings scope the session loads.

sandbox.filesystem.allowRead.description: Re-open reading for specific paths inside a region that `denyRead` blocks, to build workspace-only read access. An exact or wildcard `denyRead` entry stays blocked inside a broader `allowRead`, as the overlap table shows. When a wildcard `denyRead` entry such as `~/**/.env` matches a directory, Claude Code blocks reads of its contents as well. Before v2.1.236 on macOS, Claude Code re-opened the paths a wildcard `denyRead` entry matched wherever a broader `allowRead` entry covered them, and left a matched directory's contents readable.
sandbox.filesystem.allowRead.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes

sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite.default: unset, so sandboxed commands can write to the working directory, the per-user temp directory, directories you've added with `--add-dir` or `/add-dir`, and directories in `permissions.additionalDirectories`
sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite.description: Add paths where sandboxed commands can write, beyond the working directory, the per-user temp directory, and the directories you've added with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or `permissions.additionalDirectories`. Use it when a subprocess such as `kubectl` or a build tool needs to write outside the project.
sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes

sandbox.filesystem.denyRead.default: unset, so sandboxed commands keep the default read access, which includes credential files such as `~/.aws/credentials`
sandbox.filesystem.denyRead.description: Block sandboxed commands from reading specific paths, such as credential files that the default read policy would otherwise expose. To protect a credential file and keep it usable through the sandbox proxy, see `sandbox.credentials` instead.
sandbox.filesystem.denyRead.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes

sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite.description: Block sandboxed commands from writing to specific paths, including paths inside a directory that is otherwise writable.
sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes

sandbox.filesystem.disabled.description: Skip filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read and write access to the host filesystem, and their network egress stays confined to `network.allowedDomains`. Use it when you sandbox to control where commands connect rather than what they write.
sandbox.filesystem.disabled.scope_note: When managed settings configure `sandbox.filesystem` at all, or list a `sandbox.credentials.files` entry with `"mode": "deny"`, only managed settings can set it.

sandbox.ignoreViolations.default: unset, so every violation is reported
sandbox.ignoreViolations.description: Silence sandbox violation reports for paths you expect a command to probe and be refused, such as a tool that checks `/etc/hosts` on startup, so those denials don't show up as violations or in what Claude sees. The sandbox still blocks the access; only the report is suppressed. Keys are substrings to match against the command, with `*` matching every command, and values are substrings of the violation to ignore for that command, such as a filesystem path.
sandbox.ignoreViolations.type: object mapping a command substring to an array of violation substrings, usually paths

sandbox.network.default: unset, so no domains are pre-allowed and your permission mode decides what happens to each new host
sandbox.network.description: Control which hosts, ports, and sockets sandboxed commands can reach. The sandbox routes outbound traffic through a proxy that enforces these lists; see Network isolation for how the proxy decides and when it prompts.
sandbox.network.scope_note: `strictAllowlist`, `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, and `tlsTerminate` are read from fewer sources, as their entries say.

sandbox.network.allowAllUnixSockets.description: Let sandboxed commands connect to every Unix socket. On Linux and WSL2, the sandbox's seccomp filter blocks `socket(AF_UNIX, ...)` calls, so this is the only way to permit Unix sockets there. When the filter is missing, which `/sandbox` reports on its Dependencies tab, the sandbox doesn't block Unix-socket calls. See Set up Linux and WSL2 for where the filter comes from.

sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding.description: Let sandboxed commands on macOS listen on network ports, for example to start a dev server, and connect to any port on localhost. A command that listens on a non-loopback address accepts connections from other machines. The key has no effect on Linux and WSL2, where each sandboxed command has its own loopback interface. To reach a server on the host from Linux or WSL2, see A command fails to reach a server on localhost.

sandbox.network.allowMachLookup.description: List additional XPC and Mach service names the macOS sandbox may look up. Tools that communicate over XPC, such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright, need their services listed here. Sandboxed commands can reach outside the sandbox to each service that you list, and the sandbox doesn't confine what those services do for those commands.
sandbox.network.allowMachLookup.type: array of strings, each a service name; a single trailing `*` matches a prefix, and `"*"` alone matches every service

sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly.description: Lock the network allowlist to what managed settings define. Claude Code then honors only `allowedDomains` and `WebFetch(domain:...)` allow rules from managed settings, ignores domains from user, project, local, and `--settings` settings, and blocks a non-allowed domain automatically instead of prompting.

sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets.default: unset, so the macOS sandbox blocks every Unix socket
sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets.description: List the Unix socket paths sandboxed commands can connect to on macOS. Claude Code ignores this list on Linux and WSL2, where the seccomp filter can't inspect socket paths; use `allowAllUnixSockets` there instead.
sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets.type: array of strings, each a socket path

sandbox.network.allowedDomains.default: unset, so your permission mode decides what happens to each new host
sandbox.network.allowedDomains.description: Pre-allow domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, so the sandbox doesn't prompt for them. Wildcards such as `*.example.com` match subdomains, and an optional `:port` suffix limits an entry to one port; an entry without a port matches every port.
sandbox.network.allowedDomains.type: array of strings, each a domain, wildcard pattern, or IP literal, with an optional `:port` suffix

sandbox.network.deniedDomains.description: Block domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, using the same wildcard, port, and IPv6 syntax as `allowedDomains`. A denied domain stays blocked even when an `allowedDomains` entry matches it too.
sandbox.network.deniedDomains.type: array of strings, each a domain, wildcard pattern, or IP literal, with an optional `:port` suffix

sandbox.network.httpProxyPort.default: unset, so Claude Code runs its own proxy
sandbox.network.httpProxyPort.description: Point the sandbox at your own HTTP proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Organizations do this to inspect HTTPS traffic, apply their own filtering rules, or log requests. Your proxy takes over filtering, and Claude Code stops applying its domain lists and network prompts to traffic sent there. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for HTTP traffic.

sandbox.network.socksProxyPort.default: unset, so Claude Code runs its own proxy
sandbox.network.socksProxyPort.description: Point the sandbox at your own SOCKS5 proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Your proxy takes over filtering, and Claude Code stops applying its domain lists and network prompts to traffic sent there. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for SOCKS traffic.

sandbox.network.strictAllowlist.description: Deny sandboxed commands access to hosts outside the allowlist instead of prompting for approval. The allowlist is `allowedDomains` plus domains from `WebFetch(domain:...)` allow rules, or only the managed settings entries when `allowManagedDomainsOnly` is set. Locks that apply without an admin-required sandbox covers a repository's entries. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.
sandbox.network.strictAllowlist.scope_note: A repository can't turn it on or off.

sandbox.network.tlsTerminate.default: unset, so the proxy doesn't terminate or inspect TLS
sandbox.network.tlsTerminate.description: Make the sandbox proxy terminate TLS so it can read the contents of HTTPS requests. This is experimental, and `mask` credential substitution requires it. Set `{}` to generate an ephemeral certificate authority for the session, or set `caCertPath` and `caKeyPath` to use your own.
sandbox.network.tlsTerminate.scope_note: A repository can't switch it on or supply a certificate authority.
sandbox.network.tlsTerminate.type: object with optional `caCertPath` and `caKeyPath` strings, each a file path

sandbox.ripgrep.default: unset, so the sandbox uses the same ripgrep binary as Claude Code. That is the bundled binary unless you set `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP` to `0`
sandbox.ripgrep.description: Point the sandbox at a ripgrep binary of your own instead of the one Claude Code uses, for example when your platform needs a differently built `rg`.
sandbox.ripgrep.type: object with `command`, the path to the ripgrep binary, and optional `args`, an array of arguments to prepend

sandbox.socatPath.default: unset, so Claude Code finds `socat` on `PATH`
sandbox.socatPath.description: Point the sandbox network proxy at a `socat` binary installed outside `PATH`.
sandbox.socatPath.type: string, an absolute path; Claude Code drops a relative path and falls back to `PATH` lookup

showClearContextOnPlanAccept.description: When Claude finishes a plan in plan mode, it shows an approval menu. Planning can use a lot of context, so this key adds a first option to that menu, **Yes, clear context and …**, that approves the plan, clears the conversation context, and starts implementing from the plan alone. The rest of the label names the permission mode the session continues in, and shows how much of your context the planning used.

showThinkingSummaries.description: See summaries of Claude's extended thinking in interactive sessions. Set it if you want the full summaries when you expand thinking with `Ctrl+O`. When unset or `false`, the Anthropic API redacts thinking blocks and Claude Code shows a collapsed stub.

showTurnDuration.description: Show or hide the turn duration message after each response, such as "Cooked for 1m 6s · done 6:05 PM". The clock after "done" shows when the turn finished; `timeFormat` and `timeZone` control its format and zone. Appears in `/config` as **Show turn duration**.
showTurnDuration.scope_note: A value in `~/.claude.json` from an older version applies when no settings file sets it.

skillListingBudgetFraction.default: `0.01`, which reserves 1% of the context window
skillListingBudgetFraction.description: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills with their descriptions, and Claude Code caps that listing at a share of the context window. When the listing is over the cap, Claude Code keeps every skill's name but drops the descriptions of the least-used skills, so Claude can still invoke those skills but is less likely to choose one on its own. Raise this key to keep more descriptions visible at the cost of more context per turn.
skillListingBudgetFraction.type: number, a fraction greater than `0` and at most `1`

skillListingMaxDescChars.description: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills that shows each skill's `description` and `when_to_use` text. This key caps how many characters of that text Claude Code shows per skill; longer text is cut at the cap.
skillListingMaxDescChars.type: number of characters, a positive integer

skillOverrides.description: Hide or collapse a skill without editing its `SKILL.md`. Claude Code applies the value under each skill's name to the skill list Claude sees and to your `/` autocomplete.
skillOverrides.type: object mapping skill name to one of:

skipAutoPermissionPrompt.default: unset, so the notice appears once
skipAutoPermissionPrompt.description: Skip the one-time notice describing auto mode that Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself, for example through your own settings or the mode selector, rather than when the built-in default starts a session in it. Claude Code shows that notice once and then records that it was shown, so this key only matters where the notice hasn't appeared yet.
skipAutoPermissionPrompt.scope_note: A repository can't set it for you.

skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt.description: Skip the confirmation dialog Claude Code shows before a session enters `bypassPermissions` mode, whether from `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or from `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`. Claude Code writes `true` here in your user settings when you accept that dialog once.
skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt.scope_note: An untrusted repository can't skip the dialog for you.

skipWebFetchPreflight.default: unset, so the check runs before the first fetch to each hostname in a session
skipWebFetchPreflight.description: Skip the WebFetch domain safety check, which sends each requested hostname to `api.anthropic.com` before fetching. Set `true` in environments that block traffic to Anthropic, such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry deployments with restrictive egress.

spellcheck.default: unset, so spell checking is off; `checker` defaults to `"auto"`, the first of the three found on `PATH`; `language` defaults to the checker's own dictionary; `color` defaults to the theme's error color
spellcheck.description: Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using a spell checker you install. Claude Code checks only the text in the input box. Check spelling as you type covers installing aspell, hunspell, or ispell and what the checker covers. Requires Claude Code v2.1.235 or later.
spellcheck.scope_note: The block from the highest tier that sets it applies as a whole.
spellcheck.type: object with `enabled` (Boolean), `checker` (`"aspell"`, `"hunspell"`, `"ispell"`, or `"auto"`), `language` (string, passed to the checker as its dictionary name), and `color` (string, a terminal color name, `#rrggbb`, `rgb(r,g,b)`, `ansi256(n)`, or `ansi:<name>`)

spinnerTipsEnabled.description: While Claude works, the spinner line rotates through short tips about Claude Code features, such as "Use Plan Mode to prepare for a complex request before making changes. Press Shift+Tab twice to enable." Set this key to `false` to hide them. Appears in `/config` as **Show tips**.

spinnerTipsOverride.default: unset, so Claude Code shows only the built-in tips
spinnerTipsOverride.description: Add your own tips to the spinner tips that Claude Code shows while Claude works, or replace the built-in tips with yours. Claude Code puts your tips in the same rotation as the built-in ones.
spinnerTipsOverride.scope_note: Claude Code honors tip objects, `tipsFile`, `label`, and `excludeDefault` from user settings, the `--settings` flag, and managed settings; from project and local settings it reads plain string tips only.
spinnerTipsOverride.type: object with `tips`, `tipsFile`, `label`, and `excludeDefault` fields, each optional

spinnerVerbs.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the built-in verbs
spinnerVerbs.description: While a turn is in progress, the spinner shows a rotating verb such as "Accomplishing", "Architecting", or "Baking". Use this key to add your own verbs to that rotation or replace the built-in list with yours.
spinnerVerbs.type: object with a `verbs` array of strings and `mode`, one of:

sshConfigs.description: Add SSH connections to the Desktop environment selector. Administrators use `sshConfigs` to distribute shared connections to a team. Users can select a managed connection and set their own **Worktree folder** for it. They can't edit its other fields or delete it in the app.
sshConfigs.scope_note: The desktop app reads this key. By default, it reads managed connections from one managed source.
sshConfigs.type: array of objects, each with required `id`, `name`, and `sshHost` and optional `sshPort` and `sshIdentityFile`

sshHostAllowlist.default: unset, so any host is allowed
sshHostAllowlist.description: Limit the hosts a Desktop SSH session can connect to. Only the Desktop app reads this key; the CLI doesn't. Patterns are case-insensitive: `*` matches any host, `*.example.com` matches `example.com` and every subdomain, and anything else is an exact match against the hostname after `~/.ssh/config` resolution. An empty array turns SSH sessions off.
sshHostAllowlist.scope_note: By default, Desktop reads the key from one managed source.

sshHostCommands.description: Add SSH connections whose host comes from a command to the Desktop environment selector. When you create a connection or create another machine for it, Desktop runs the entry's command on your computer and connects to the host that the command prints.
sshHostCommands.scope_note: Only the desktop app reads this key. It reads managed entries from one managed settings file or MDM policy on the computer, and ignores the key in server-managed settings.
sshHostCommands.type: array of objects, each with required `id`, `name`, and `command` and optional `sshIdentityFile` and `startDirectory`. Desktop doesn't read `command` as shell syntax, so pipes and variables don't work: write it as a program and its arguments.

statusLine.description: Run your own command to render a status line below the prompt with context such as the model, cost, or git branch. Optional fields adjust spacing, add periodic re-runs, and hide the built-in vim mode indicator when your script renders `vim.mode` itself.
statusLine.scope_note: When `allowManagedHooksOnly` is on, or `disableAllHooks` is set outside managed settings, only the managed settings value runs.
statusLine.type: object with `type` set to `"command"` and a `command` string, plus optional `padding` as a number of characters, `refreshInterval` as a number of seconds, minimum `1`, and `hideVimModeIndicator` as a Boolean

strictKnownMarketplaces.default: unset, so users can add any marketplace. An empty array is a complete lockdown that blocks every marketplace source, including the official Anthropic marketplace
strictKnownMarketplaces.description: Restrict which plugin marketplace sources people in your organization can add and install plugins from. Claude Code enforces the allowlist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, before any network or filesystem operation, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins once its source no longer matches. Blocked users see an error naming the managed policy.
strictKnownMarketplaces.type: array of marketplace source objects; see Allowed source types

strictPluginOnlyCustomization.description: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can come only from plugins or managed settings. Combine it with `strictKnownMarketplaces` to control the full customization supply chain: the marketplace allowlist controls which plugins users can install.
strictPluginOnlyCustomization.type: `true` to lock all four kinds of customization, or an array naming the kinds to lock, from `"skills"`, `"agents"`, `"hooks"`, and `"mcp"`

strictPluginOnlyCustomization.agents.description: Lock the `agents` surface. Claude Code stops loading agents from `~/.claude/agents/`, `.claude/agents/`, and `--add-dir` directories. It keeps loading built-in agents, agents in the managed policy directory, and agents from plugins other than skills-directory plugins.

strictPluginOnlyCustomization.mcp.description: Lock the `mcp` surface. Claude Code stops loading MCP servers from `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json`. It keeps loading `managed-mcp.json` servers, servers from `managedMcpServers`, and MCP servers from plugins other than skills-directory plugins.

strictPluginOnlyCustomization.skills.description: Lock the `skills` surface. Claude Code stops loading skills from `~/.claude/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`, custom commands from `~/.claude/commands/` and `.claude/commands/`, skills and commands under `--add-dir` directories, and skills synced from your claude.ai account. It keeps loading bundled skills, skills in the managed policy directory, and skills from plugins other than skills-directory plugins.

subagentPromptCacheTtl.default: unset, so each of these requests gets its default lifetime
subagentPromptCacheTtl.description: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the requests Claude Code makes outside the main conversation. This key applies to subagents, workflows, and Claude Code's own background and helper requests, such as compaction and session titles. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

subagentStatusLine.default: unset, so Claude Code renders the default rows
subagentStatusLine.description: When Claude runs subagents, Claude Code lists them in a task display below the prompt, one row per subagent showing `name · description · token count`. This key lets you run your own command to rewrite those rows, for example to show each subagent's context usage as a percentage. On each refresh, Claude Code sends the visible rows as one JSON object on stdin, with a `tasks` array carrying each subagent's `id`, `name`, `status`, `model`, `tokenCount`, and more, and replaces the row for each `id` you write back as a `{"id", "content"}` line. Rows you don't write back keep the default rendering.
subagentStatusLine.scope_note: When `allowManagedHooksOnly` is on, or `disableAllHooks` is set outside managed settings, only the managed settings value runs.
subagentStatusLine.type: object with `type` set to `"command"` and a `command` string

switchModelsOnFlag.default: unset. Claude Code switches automatically, though it may ask first in an interactive session
switchModelsOnFlag.description: Choose what happens when a safety classifier flags a request: switch to the fallback model and continue, or pause so you can choose between switching and editing the prompt.
switchModelsOnFlag.scope_note: Appears in `/config` as **Switch models when a message is flagged**, with the options **Switch automatically** and **Ask each time**.

syncClaudeAiPlugins.default: unset, so sessions signed in with your claude.ai account sync your plugins
syncClaudeAiPlugins.description: Turn off the download of the plugins enabled for your claude.ai account. Claude Code downloads them into `~/.claude/plugins/synced/` at the start of terminal sessions where you sign in with your claude.ai account and in Cowork sessions, and loads each one as `<name>@synced`. Set `false` to stop that download and stop loading the plugins it already synced. Claude Code honors only `false`: `true` is the same as unset and doesn't turn syncing on where it's otherwise off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.273 or later.
syncClaudeAiPlugins.scope_note: A repository can't turn it off for you.

syncClaudeAiSkills.default: unset, so sessions signed in with your claude.ai account sync your skills
syncClaudeAiSkills.description: Turn off the download of the skills enabled for your claude.ai account. Claude Code downloads them into `~/.claude/skills/synced/` in terminal sessions where you sign in with your claude.ai account, interactive or non-interactive, and in Cowork and cloud sessions. Set `false` to stop that download and stop loading the skills it already synced. Claude Code honors only `false`: `true` is the same as unset and doesn't turn syncing on where it's otherwise off.
syncClaudeAiSkills.scope_note: A repository can't turn it off for you.

syntaxHighlightingDisabled.description: Claude Code colors code by language in the diffs, code blocks, and file previews it shows in the terminal, with its built-in highlighter; no plugin or language server is involved. Set this key to `true` to show them as plain text instead, for example if the colors clash with your terminal theme or slow a screen reader.

taskOutputMaxChars.description: > [!WARNING] > > Removed in v2.1.277, together with the `TaskOutput` tool it sized. Setting it has no effect on current versions. Claude reads a background task's output file with `Read` instead.

teammateDefaultModel.description: > [!WARNING] > > Removed in v2.1.234, together with its `/config` row **Default teammate model**. Setting it has no effect on current versions.
teammateDefaultModel.type: string, a model alias or full model ID, or `null`

teammateMode.description: Choose where Claude Code shows agent team teammates: inside your main terminal pane, or in split panes when your terminal supports them. See Choose a display mode.
teammateMode.scope_note: Claude Code also reads a value left in `~/.claude.json` by older versions.

terminalProgressBarEnabled.description: Some terminals can show a progress indicator on the tab or in the taskbar for the program running in them. While Claude is working, Claude Code reports an in-progress state to the terminal, so you can see from another tab or window whether the session is still busy. The indicator stays visible after the turn ends while background subagents or dynamic workflows are still running, and clears once the session is idle.
terminalProgressBarEnabled.scope_note: A value in `~/.claude.json` from an older version applies when no settings file sets it.

terminalTitleFromRename.description: Claude Code sets your terminal tab's title. By default it uses a title it generates from the conversation, and once you give the session a name with `/rename` or `--name`, the tab shows that name instead. Set this key to `false` to keep the generated title on the tab even after you name the session. The name itself still applies, so `/resume <name>` and the session picker find it.

theme.description: Pick the color theme for the interface. Appears in `/config` as **Theme**.
theme.scope_note: A value in `~/.claude.json` from an older version applies when no settings file sets it.

timeFormat.description: Choose how Claude Code writes the times it shows in the interface, such as the `done 6:05 PM` at the end of each turn duration message and the timestamps in the transcript viewer. To pick a preset, run `/config` and set **Time format**. Requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.

timeZone.default: unset, so times show in your system time zone
timeZone.description: Show the times in the interface in a time zone other than your system's. Set it to an IANA time zone name, such as `"UTC"` or `"Europe/Dublin"`. The times that `timeFormat` controls then show in this zone. If `timeFormat` is `"24-hour-utc"`, times stay in UTC and Claude Code ignores this key. `/config` has no row for this key, so set it in a settings file. Requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.
timeZone.type: string, an IANA time zone name. When Claude Code doesn't recognize the name, it uses your system time zone

tui.default: unset, so Claude Code picks the renderer for you
tui.description: Choose the terminal UI renderer. Use `"fullscreen"` for the flicker-free alt-screen renderer with virtualized scrollback, or `"default"` for the classic main-screen renderer. Running `/tui fullscreen` or `/tui default` writes this key for you.

ultracode.description: Start sessions with ultracode on. With it on, Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task instead of waiting for you to ask. Claude plans workflows only when dynamic workflows are enabled for you and your model supports `xhigh` effort. The key doesn't change the session's effort level: ultracode runs at whichever level the session uses. Claude Code reads this key but never writes it: `/effort ultracode` turns ultracode on for the current session only.

useAutoModeDuringPlan.description: Choose whether Claude Code uses the auto mode classifier to review shell commands in plan mode. With the default `true`, the classifier reviews each command during planning when auto mode is available and you see no prompt, except for critical-path removals. Set `false` to get a permission prompt for every command outside the built-in read-only set. Appears in `/config` as **Use auto mode during plan**.
useAutoModeDuringPlan.scope_note: A repository can't turn it off for you.

verbose.description: By default, the transcript collapses each tool call to a short summary, such as the command Claude ran and a line count of its output, and you press `Ctrl+O` to switch the whole transcript to the expanded view when you want the details. Set this key to `true` to show every tool call's full input and output inline as it happens, which is useful when you're debugging a hook, an MCP server, or a long shell command. Appears in `/config` as **Verbose output**.
verbose.scope_note: A value in `~/.claude.json` from an older version applies when no settings file sets it.

viewMode.default: unset, so the `verbose` setting and your last `/focus` choice apply
viewMode.description: Set the transcript view Claude Code starts in: `"default"`, `"verbose"`, or `"focus"`. When set, it overrides both the sticky `/focus` selection and the `verbose` setting.

vimInsertModeRemaps.description: Map two-key INSERT-mode sequences to Escape in vim editor mode. Each key is exactly two printable characters typed in sequence, and `"<Esc>"` is the only supported target; Claude Code ignores other entries.
vimInsertModeRemaps.scope_note: A repository can't remap your keystrokes.
vimInsertModeRemaps.type: object mapping a two-character sequence to `"<Esc>"`

voice.default: unset, so dictation is off; when `enabled` is `true` and `mode` is unset, Claude Code uses `"hold"`
voice.description: Turn on voice dictation and choose how the dictation key behaves. Claude Code writes this object for you when you run `/voice`.
voice.type: object with `enabled` as a Boolean, `autoSubmit` as a Boolean that applies in hold mode only, and `mode`, one of:

voiceEnabled.description: > [!WARNING] > > Deprecated since v2.1.92, when the `voice` object replaced it. Claude Code still reads it so older settings files keep working, but new configurations should set `voice.enabled`.

wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled.description: Accelerate mouse-wheel scroll speed during fast scrolls in fullscreen rendering. Set it to `false` for a constant scroll rate per wheel notch.

workflowKeywordTriggerEnabled.description: Choose whether typing the keyword `ultracode` in a prompt triggers a dynamic workflow. Set it to `false` to type the word without triggering one.

workflowSizeGuideline.default: `"medium"`, or `"small"` when you're signed in on a Pro plan with Claude Code v2.1.271 or later
workflowSizeGuideline.description: Set the agent count Claude aims for in the dynamic workflows it writes. Claude Code sends the value to Claude as advice, not an enforced cap: `"small"` asks for fewer than 5 agents, `"medium"` fewer than 10, and `"large"` fewer than 50. Choose `"small"` when you want to bound what a workflow spends.
workflowSizeGuideline.scope_note: A value there takes precedence over the **Dynamic workflow size** choice in `/config`, which Claude Code stores in `~/.claude.json`, and Claude Code hides that row while a settings file sets the key.

worktree.description: Configure how Claude Code creates and manages git worktrees for `--worktree`, the `EnterWorktree` tool, and isolated subagents and background sessions.

worktree.baseRef.description: Choose which ref new worktrees branch from. `"fresh"` branches from `origin/<default-branch>` for a clean tree matching the remote; `"head"` branches from your current local `HEAD`, so unpushed commits and feature-branch state are present in the worktree.

worktree.bgIsolation.description: Choose how background sessions isolate their file edits. If you moved a session to the background with `←` or `/background`, that session edits files in place whatever this key says. With `"worktree"`, Claude Code blocks `Edit` and `Write` in the main checkout until the session calls `EnterWorktree`; with `"none"`, background jobs edit the working copy directly. Set `"none"` for a repository where git worktrees are impractical.

worktree.location.default: unset, so worktrees go inside the project
worktree.location.description: Choose the folder on a remote machine where Desktop SSH sessions create their worktrees, instead of `<project-root>/.claude/worktrees/`. Only the desktop app reads this key: `--worktree`, the `EnterWorktree` tool, isolated subagents, and background sessions ignore it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.44121.0 or later.
worktree.location.type: string, an absolute path or one that starts with `~/`

worktree.sparsePaths.default: unset, so each worktree checks out the whole tree
worktree.sparsePaths.description: Check out only the listed directories in each worktree through git sparse-checkout. Claude Code writes only those directories plus root-level files to disk, which is faster in large monorepos; see Check out only the directories you need.
worktree.sparsePaths.type: array of strings, directory paths relative to the repository root

worktree.symlinkDirectories.default: unset, so Claude Code symlinks no directories

wslInheritsWindowsSettings.description: Have Claude Code on WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain, with HKLM and the Windows managed settings file taking priority over `/etc/claude-code` and HKCU below it. While the chain is on, Claude Code reads `/etc/claude-code` only when no Windows admin document is present in the HKLM registry value or the `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\` folder. Set it to extend the policy you already deploy on Windows to WSL sessions on the same machine, so they follow the same rules as host sessions. Claude Code honors it only when set in the HKLM registry key or in a managed settings file or drop-in under `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`, both of which require Windows admin to write.
